subject: Career
title: Strategic Timing: When to Act
description: A 60-second lesson on Strategic Timing: When to Act.

hook.text: She waited three months to propose the reorganization — until after the Q3 numbers proved her point.

buildup.text: In politics, timing is everything. The same proposal succeeds or fails depending on when it's introduced.

discovery.text: John Kingdon's 'policy windows' theory: change happens when a problem, solution, and political will converge.

twist.text: Pushing an idea too early meets resistance. Too late and someone else gets credit. The window is narrow.

climax.text: Watch for triggers: budget season, leadership changes, crises, or big wins. These open windows for proposals.

punchline.text: Right idea, wrong time = rejected. Right idea, right time = adopted.

quiz.question: What is a 'policy window' according to Kingdon's theory?
options: When a problem, solution, and political will converge for change
A window in a government office

details.summary: Political timing involves choosing the optimal moment to propose changes, make requests, or escalate issues. The same initiative can succeed or fail based entirely on when it is presented relative to organizational mood, budget cycles, and leadership priorities.
details.whyItMatters: Good ideas at the wrong time get rejected. Understanding organizational rhythms and windows of opportunity maximizes the impact of your political capital.
takeaways: Propose initiatives when leadership is focused on related priorities
Budget season and strategic planning cycles create natural windows
Avoid major asks during crisis periods when attention is elsewhere

faq.question: How do you identify the right moment to pitch an idea to leadership?
faq.answer: Align your pitch with a current organizational pain point or strategic theme. Watch for moments when leaders publicly express frustration with a problem your idea solves. Post-crisis windows, when organizations are seeking improvements, are also powerful timing opportunities.

faq.question: Is there a worst time to make a significant career request?
faq.answer: Avoid major asks during active crises, immediately after poor financial results, or when your manager is visibly stressed by unrelated problems. Also avoid Mondays and late Fridays when energy and receptivity tend to be lowest.
